decisions.reason: Case report of colloid cyst confined to the velum interpositum; full PubMed abstract only says location 'gives additional information on pathogenesis' and briefly reviews pathogenesis, never naming a paraphyseal or other specific origin; no histogenesis data shown. Excluded as clinical case without verifiable paraphysis/histogenesis content (full text would show whether paraphyseal origin is argued).

Craniate character 93 'Paraphysis' is explicitly applied to the left epithalamic (parapineal) diverticulum vs right epiphysis, not the telencephalic paraphysis; kept as necessary context for the phylogeny/terminology section because this homonymous usage would contaminate any reported distribution of 'paraphysis' (lampreys, actinopterygians, sarcopterygians). No data on the telencephalic paraphysis.

Metadata-only official embryological nomenclature; no paraphysis or telencephalon impar entry confirmed and title is non-specific. Cannot support inclusion; checking TE2 telencephalon/roof entries for 'paraphysis' would resolve.

Only a table-of-contents line seen for a general lungfish CNS chapter; title does not name the paraphysis/dorsal sac/coronarium and coverage is unverified. Excluded for lack of evidence (chapter text or index for paraphysis/dorsal sac/telencephalic roof would resolve).

Full abstract checked: adult Xenopus Pax6/Pax7 map, only Pax6 in telencephalon (olfactory bulbs, septum, striatum, amygdala); no mention of paraphysis, telencephalic roof or midline; generic marker map with no link to the paraphysis region.

Metadata-only official neuroanatomical nomenclature; finder confirmed unit pages for tela choroidea and suprapineal recess but no paraphysis entry; nothing verifiable to support inclusion (direct TNA term search for paraphysis would resolve).

Metadata-only veterinary embryological nomenclature PDF; no excerpt, paraphysis entry unverified and title non-specific. Excluded (text search of the NEV PDF for paraphysis/telencephalon impar would resolve).

Case of paired third-ventricle colloid cysts whose stated purpose is a discussion of embryological origin ('re-ignites the debate' on origin); this is the histogenesis debate (endodermal/neuroepithelial/paraphyseal) needed to weigh the paraphyseal hypothesis for the clinical correlate. Whether paraphysis is explicitly argued is unverified (web snippet only), so B rather than A.

Comparative review of ventricular system development; the excerpt covers zebrafish circumventricular organs and choroid plexus and never names paraphysis, dorsal sac or velum transversum. Generic CVO/choroid plexus content that cannot be shown to bear on the paraphysis; full-text search for 'paraphysis' would be needed to reverse.

Japanese single operated case of third-ventricle ependymal cyst with literature review; metadata only, title does not name the paraphysis or paraphyseal cyst and no abstract seen. Treated as a clinical case series without verifiable histogenesis content (abstract/text would show whether paraphyseal origin is discussed).

Lexicon definition of telencephalon impar: median, non-evaginated telencephalon around the interventricular foramen in the former roof and floor plate territory, i.e. the region that locates the paraphysis (ontogeny/anatomy/terminology). Paraphysis is not named and the source is tertiary (cites Sobotta), so a necessary-context definition only.

Classical (1888) development-of-the-epiphysis paper; Dexter 1902 credits Francotte with first identifying the paraphysis in a 12-week human embryo and with holding that it occurs in all vertebrate embryos, and the paper is listed in Warren's 1905 paraphysis/pineal-region bibliography. Included as historical record; content unverified (metadata only) and the exact carrying paper rests on Dexter's attribution.

Metadata-only catalogue entry for a multi-volume comparative treatise (diencephalon and telencephalon derivatives); no evidence it treats the paraphysis, and no independent link to the paraphysis literature. Excluded rather than rewarding the treatise's stature (index/ToC check for paraphysis, dorsal sac, telencephalon impar would resolve).

Classical comparative anatomy and development of the craniate forebrain (Studnicka), cited in Warren's 1905 bibliography on paraphysis and pineal region development; needed for ontogeny/homology of the telencephalic roof and median telencephalon in which the paraphysis arises. Content unverified (metadata only), so B not A.
